ai.description: *Boiga multifasciata* reaches 1.2 m. It is pale brown with 30–40 dark brown crossbands and a distinct dark postocular stripe. It features a slender, laterally compressed body and large, prominent eyes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Boiga multifasciata* is best distinguished by its distinct, narrow black cross-bands that extend onto the belly, contrasting with the uniform or spotted venters of similar species.
ai.habitat: *Boiga multifasciata* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests across the Himalayas and Northeast India, typically found at altitudes between 500 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Many-banded Tree Snake is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights actively hunting for lizards and small mammals among the branches of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Boiga multifasciata* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 5–12 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing by late summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Boiga multifasciata* is found in the Himalayan foothills of Northeast India, ranging from Uttarakhand through West Bengal and Assam at elevations up to 2,000 meters.
